 LIVE Updated 1 min ago Anthropic IPO live: Company prices stock at $83, set to begin trading today
 Daniel Howley · Technology Editor Updated Thu, November 19, 2026 at 10:06 AM EST 1 min read ANT 0.00% 
 Anthropic ( ANT ) priced its IPO at $83 per share, ahead of its trading debut today. That's above earlier estimates of $80. The outlet previously reported that shares were oversubscribed by as much as 6x. 
 Anthropic, which Yahoo Finance named its Company of the Year for 2026 , reported in its most recent amended S-1 that its third-quarter revenue climbed to $17 billion, a 12x year over year increase. 
 For the nine months that ended Sept. 30, Anthropic's sales eclipsed $33 billion. It brought in $2.5 billion in all of 2025 and just $41 million in 2023. 
 Anthropic's sales continue to improve. Its number of customers spending more than $100,000 has increased from roughly 1,500 in December 2025 to more than 11,900 as of Sept. 30. Its computing efficiency has also jumped, meaning it's seeing more revenue per dollar spent on computing infrastructure. 
 "There's no real historical analogy for a company that has been this successful this fast," NYU Stern School of Business professor Arun Sundararajan told Yahoo Finance. 
 Anthropic's public debut also comes amid a wave of upheaval in the AI industry, ranging from market jitters to questions about the technology's impact on jobs. 
 It also faces plenty of competition from rival OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ), as well as heavy hitters like Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) and Meta ( META ). 
 Now the market will determine how that risk factors into the company's future prospects. 
 LIVE 41 updates 1 min ago Jared Blikre Anthropic goes public as AI bug hunters push cybersecurity stocks higher
 Anthropic's debut is the AI payday Wall Street has been waiting for. For the companies that fix broken software, the whole year has been a Y2K -style bonanza. 
 Anthropic ( ANT ) priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70-$78 range. It arrives after weeks of outages at Microsoft ( MSFT ), JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) and Apple ( AAPL ), each blamed on internal problems rather than hackers. 
 Ben Emons of research firm FedWatch Advisors calls it the "Patchpocalypse." "A flood of AI-found bugs means a flood of patches, and every patch is a chance for something to break," he wrote Wednesday. 
 Newly reported software security flaws in the federal National Vulnerability Database hit a record high of almost 17,500 in October, about four times the level a year earlier, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. This year's count, more than 100,000, already tops 2024 and 2025 combined. 
 Stock price change from the April 7 close, the day Anthropic announced Claude Mythos Preview, through the Nov. 18 close · Yahoo Finance R ead more . 
 5 mins ago Daniel Howley Anthropic president Daniela Amodei says what people to choose to build with AI is up to 'all of us'
 "To anyone watching who is uneasy about AI or unsure what it will mean for you. This technology needs you. Not your trust, not your use, but your voice," Anthropic ( ANT ) president Daniela Amodei said. 
 "The end of the story isn't written yet. Intelligence is now something humans can build. What we choose to build with it is up to all of us," she added. 
 5 mins ago Ines Ferré Anthropic shares indicated to open at $100 each
 Initial indications suggest Anthropic shares could open at $100 each, about 20% above the AI developer's IPO price of $83 a piece. 
 7 mins ago Ines Ferré Anthropic IPO gives boost to AI trade
 Stocks soared on Thursday as Anthropic's ( ANT ) founders rang the opening bell on the Nasdaq, and investors awaited the first trade on one of the most widely anticipated IPO's of the AI boom. The AI developer priced its IPO at $83 per share. 
 Nearly every corner of the AI trade rose, with semiconductor stocks leading the way. Shares of optical and laser equipment makers, as well as neocloud providers, also gained, helping to send the Tech ( XLK ) sector higher.

 9 mins ago Daniel Howley Anthropic president Daniela Amodei speaks at the Nasdaq
 "Our goal is to help the world make smart choices in setting the rules that govern AI and in shaping how people put it to use," Anthropic ( ANT ) president Daniela Amodei said at a speech at the Nasdaq in Times Square. 
 "More than half of the Fortune 500 use Claude for everything from drug discovery to underwriting to preventing financial fraude and abuse. 
 We want Claude to be a trusted partner, one that's honest with you, one that makes you more capable, but one that leaves you in charge. Plenty of technology is built to take up your time, we want Claude to give it back to you." 
 13 mins ago David Hollerith Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley set to reap $113 million from Anthropic IPO
 Goldman Sachs ( GS ) and Morgan Stanley ( MS ) could each collect roughly $113 million in fees for leading Anthropic's ( ANT ) initial public offering on Thursday. 
 The estimates, which exceed the $100 million windfall the two Wall Street banks earned from SpaceX's ( SPCX ) June listing, are based on the banks' underwriting commitments of 20.5% of the $81.3 billion public offering, according to Anthropic's regulatory prospectus filed Thursday morning. 
 Follow live updates of Anthropic's IPO here. 
 JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) and Citigroup ( C ) each committed to underwrite 10% of the offering, equivalent to approximately $55 million apiece if fees are distributed proportionately. Bank of America ( BAC ) committed to 3%, or about $16.5 million. 
 The $550 million fee pool is among the largest in IPO history, approaching the approximately $550.2 million banks collected from Visa's 2008 offering. It also exceeds the roughly $500 million in commissions generated by Elon Musk's SpaceX IPO in June. 
 Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley each collected approximately $100 million from that deal . Read more .

 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei spoke about AI safety before ringing the opening bell this morning. 
 37 mins ago Daniel Howley Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and president Daniela Amodei ring opening bell
 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and president Daniela Amodei are ringing the opening bell at the Nasdaq on Thursday, as the company prepares for its first trade as a public company. 
 Shares are priced at $83, above the initial range. 
 Anthropic will provide a test of the AI market and how investors view its stability and growth prospects. 
 41 mins ago Yahoo Finance What price will Anthropic shares open? YF takes a guess
 Yahoo Finance anchors take a stab at ANT's opening trade. 
 Today at 2:01 PM UTC Yahoo Finance The AI revolution gets its first pure-play public lab: Yorkville Ives
 In a note to investors, Dan Ives weighs in on ANT's IPO: 
 "At a time when investors are very nervous about the overall tech trade and the Nvidia black cloud moment casts a shadow over the tech sector, Anthropic's IPO is a big near-term win for the tech sector and should help restore some investor confidence that the AI Revolution growth thesis is not waning. It is going through a very turbulent, white-knuckle period that does not change our longer-term view that $3 trillion to $4 trillion of capex will be spent over the next few years on the AI Revolution, and this sets the stage for the next phase of tech and infrastructure investment with Anthropic a central player in the buildout." 
 Today at 2:00 PM UTC Hal Bundrick, CFP® Anthropic in your 401(k) or IRA? How you could get exposure after its IPO.
 Anthropic's IPO could open new ways to invest in AI through retirement accounts. Here's what to know. 
 Allocating Anthropic IPO shares in an IRA 
 If you meet the eligibility standards, the brokerages sponsoring the Anthropic IPO may allow you to request that IPO shares be allocated to your IRA. However, some brokers prohibit retirement accounts from IPO access. Two of the major brokers offering the Anthropic IPO are Fidelity and Schwab. 
 While neither brokerage gave details on their IPO information pages about holding IPO shares in a retirement account, Fidelity's customer service confirmed that shares could be held in an IRA. A Schwab live chat representative also said that Anthropic shares could be allocated to an IRA. 
 If your account is held by another broker that is offering the IPO, check whether an allocation of shares can be made to an IRA account. 
 Getting indirect exposure to an IPO 
 Retirement investors can also get indirect exposure to pre-IPO and IPO stocks by investing in certain other companies, according to Talley. 
 "For example, Microsoft has a large position in OpenAI that will cause it to profit handsomely when OpenAI goes public," Talley told Yahoo Finance. "Similarly, public pension funds often have investments in private capital markets, including pre-IPO stocks. There are several ETF products in various stages of development that may also give exposure to retail investors of a portfolio of privately owned companies, but that is still in early stages." 
 Will Anthropic shares find their way into your 401(k)? 
 Most employer-sponsored 401(k) plans limit participant investment choices to mutual funds, target-date funds, and index-based investments. However, a few plans have a self-directed option that allows individual stock and bond purchases. 
 Self-employed 401(k)s, particularly for single-owner companies, may have more investment options, and some plans may allow individual stock investments. 
 Contact your plan sponsor to confirm self-directed investing options. 
 For the majority of 401(k) plan participants, Anthropic IPO shares will enter the investment mix only as a small component of an index fund. 
 "Most index investors, for example, hold a chunk of Microsoft or Google or Oracle, which themselves have significant company-level investments in private companies, especially in the AI space," Talley said. "Indeed, retail investors may not realize how much exposure they have, especially in light of the large number of 'circular financing' deals that involve both public and nonpublic companies."  Today at 1:48 PM UTC Daniel Howley Citizens initiates coverage
 Citizens initiated coverage of Anthropic Thursday as the AI company prepares for its public markets debut. 
 Analyst Patrick Walravens put a price target of $125 on the company with a Market-Outperform rating. 
 In a note to investors, Walravens wrote that Anthropic benefits from its singular mission to develop AI for the benefit of humanity, its strong management team, its approach to safety, and its use of multiple computing sources to train and run its models. 
 Though he also notes that risks include the fact that its models have gone rogue in the past and may do so in the future. 
 Today at 1:00 PM UTC Brian Sozzi Is the AI party over? Anthropic is about to find out.
 Today is supposed to be a celebration of AI. Anthropic ( ANT ) is heading toward its long-awaited IPO at the Nasdaq , potentially giving Wall Street one of the biggest new pure-play AI investment stories in years. 
 Before you hit me up on X , Elon Musk-led SpaceX ( SPCX ) is not a pure-play AI company. It's an industrial company with a whole lot of AI bolted on. 
 But there's a problem amid all the Anthropic IPO hoopla. 
 The very stocks that fueled this AI boom are still under pressure. Just look at the sell-offs this week in top tech names like CoreWeave ( CRWV ), Salesforce ( CRM ), and even AMD ( AMD ). 
 Investors are questioning the AI spending, the valuations, the financing arrangements — and whether the returns will ever justify the billions being poured into this technology. 
 And the timing couldn't be more fascinating. 
 Truist chief market strategist Keith Lerner noted that tech valuations have fallen 42% over the past year. The sector has gone from outperforming the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) by 25% over six months to underperforming it by 6%. Bank of America's latest fund manager survey shows investors have cut tech exposure by the most since June 2006. 
 Read more . 
 Today at 12:36 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Anthropic raises $81.3 billion in record-breaking IPO
 Anthropic ( ANT ) raised $81.3 billion in its initial public offering, surpassing SpaceX's ( SPCX ) record-breaking $75 billion raised. 
 SpaceX landed with a higher valuation — $1.7 trillion — than Anthropic's valuation of over $1.5 trillion. 
 The Claude maker sold 980 million shares of Class A common stock at $83 apiece. 956,351,354 of those shares were sold by Anthropic, and 23,648,646 were sold by certain selling stockholders. Like SpaceX, Anthropic has the option to issue an additional 147 million shares within the next 30 days. 
 Today at 12:00 PM UTC Jared Blikre What 400 years of hot IPOs say about buying Anthropic on day one
 Anthropic's roadshow is selling the future of AI. Four centuries of hot IPOs say the first trade is rarely the best one. 
 The AI lab is asking for over $1.5 trillion at $83,  counting every possible share . Trading is expected to start today. Rival OpenAI ( OPAI.PRV ) may not be far behind: OpenAI president Greg Brockman said earlier this month the company could be ready to go public next year. 
 History has a warning for anyone planning to buy on the first day . The world's first IPO, the Dutch East India Company, began trading in 1602. Its stock took about three decades to double . 
 This year brought two fresh reminders. SpaceX ( SPCX ) opened at $150 in June, $15 above its IPO price, and soared about 40% in its first week. By August, it was in a nearly 30% hole. Five months later, SpaceX is still below its first trade. 
 Cerebras ( CBRS ) had it worse. The AI chipmaker opened at nearly double its $185 IPO price in May. Its first close is still its best, and the stock now trades at about half what IPO buyers paid. 
 The price tag problem 
 Anthropic's growth is anything but typical. Revenue in the first nine months of the year was 13 times what it was a year earlier. But investors are being asked to pay up for it. At $78 a share, Anthropic would trade at about 29 times its sales over the past year, by Yahoo Finance calculations. 
 University of Florida professor Jay Ritter tracked more than 4,000 IPOs of companies with at least $100 million in sales since 1980. Those priced at 20 to 40 times sales gained about 3% on average over three years from their first close. The cheapest gained about 41%. 
 There's a bright spot for Anthropic. IPOs of the biggest companies, those with more than $1 billion in sales, did about as well as the market. Read more . 
 Today at 11:00 AM UTC Brian Sozzi Anthropic's IPO day will test the AI trade. But what happens next matters more.
 The response in the days and weeks after Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) looming initial public offering will be more important to the broader AI ecosystem than the IPO itself, according to former longtime Cisco ( CSCO ) CEO and JC2 Ventures founder John Chambers. 
 "I think more important than what [the stock] comes out at is, after the IPO is out, do we see steady gains in terms of this stock and therefore encouraging others to go public and follow forward on it?" Chambers said on Sozzi Unleashed . 
 Given the rising concerns about the health of the AI ecosystem, it's a coin flip as to how Anthropic's debut on public markets will go — and what the days after will look like. 
 Today at 10:00 AM UTC Brian Sozzi Here's the cash windfall the Anthropic IPO may bring to banks like Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan and Morgan Stanley
 It stands to be a bountiful holiday quarter for some of the world's biggest banks, courtesy of the gift-giving team at Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ). 
 Using the SpaceX IPO fee rate, allocations, and a range of potential proceeds, EvercoreISI analyst Glenn Schorr estimates Anthropic's offering could generate a roughly $562 million equity capital markets (ECM) fee pool. That would equal about 1% of fourth-quarter consensus EPS across the banks he covers. 
 In Schorr's base case, co-lead underwriters Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley would each haul in $112 million in fees. Bank of America, Citigroup, and JPMorgan would each rake in $84 million. 
 A total of 22 banks appear on Anthropic's IPO tombstone, an advertisement recognizing the investment banks and other financial firms helping take the company public. 
 "A successful listing could also encourage more AI companies to test the public markets, accelerate broader IPO momentum, and reinforce the view that the AI trade still has room to run," Schorr added. Read more . 
 Today at 9:00 AM UTC Brian Sozzi What Robinhood's CFO found interesting about Anthropic's IPO prospectus
 Robinhood ( HOOD ) CFO Shiv Verma sat down with Yahoo Finance executive editor to discuss Antropic's IPO prospectus. 
 "I have gone through it. The growth rates are pretty incredible, … up 1,300% year over year, I can't recall seeing another company doing that well," Verma said on Yahoo Finance about what caught his attention from the prospectus. 
 "The other thing I thought was interesting is they were showing what percentage of their customers are in different buckets," Verma added. "And so if you spend more than $10 million a year, you're a top 250 customer. I thought that was a pretty interesting stat, as I thought it'd be a little bit larger, but it just goes to show you how big their future TAM [total addressable market] is." 
 Today at 8:00 AM UTC Brian Sozzi Why CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz is looking forward to Anthropic and OpenAI going public
 CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) founder and CEO George Kurtz said he can't wait for Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) and OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) to become public companies, as doing so will force them to act more honorably. 
 "I think when you're a public company, you have a different standard. And I know that as a public company for many years," Kurtz said at Yahoo Finance Invest. "So I'm actually looking forward to them being public, because I think the level of transparency has to go up. They're going to have to be more diligent in what happens. You just can't have these agents escape and say 'whoops.' And you're going to have to work very closely with the security companies, because you can't have the church and state, you can't use your own technology to prevent against what happens. Because when you have a failure in your own technology, you can't just say 'whoops.' So you're going to need checks and balances." 
 Kurtz added, "I think the public market is going to force that level of clarity, transparency, to make sure that A) we understand what's happening, and B) they're operating at a higher level of safety than they are today."
